targets.speaker: ALEX
targets.target: Is the product the agent, or the power to decide what the agent is allowed to do?

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: The simple version is this: who can approve, access, trigger, delete, escalate, or spend when an AI agent starts acting.

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: The scary part is not the average result. It is the person, patient, team, or company living inside the exception.

targets.speaker: RUFUS
targets.target: Lovely. We have automated the decision and preserved the blame. Very efficient, in the bleakest possible sense.

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: Think of it like the remote control for what an AI agent is allowed to touch, approve, buy, or break.

targets.speaker: ALEX
targets.target: Do not ask only what launched. Ask what new permission, risk, cost, or accountability chain just appeared.

targets.speaker: RUFUS
targets.target: The question for tomorrow is not whether permission layer sounds clever. It is who gets caught when it becomes real.
